RECIPROCAL - The product of two reciprocal numbers is 1. The reciprocal of a number is 1 over the number.
The sine of an angle is the value of the opposite side over the hypotenuse.
cosecant q = csc q = = = s q = b/c = adj/hyp
The cosecant identity is proven by rewriting the statement for sine q..
Since the hypotenuse over the opposite side is the cosecant of an angle, cosecant q is 1/sine q.
cosecant q = csc q = = = s q = b/c = adj/hyp
The secant identity is proven the same way.
cosecant q = csc q = = = s q = b/c = adj/hyp
Since the hypotenuse over the adjacent side is the secant of an angle, secant q is 1/cosine q.
cosecant q = csc q = = = s q = b/c = adj/hyp
Since the adjacent over the opposite is the cotangent of an angle, cotangent q is 1/tangent q.
cosecant q = csc q = = = s q = b/c = adj/hyp
The remaining three reciprocal identities can be proven in the same way.
cosecant q = csc q = = = s q = b/c = adj/hyp

PYTHAGOREAN & RELATED IDENTITIES
These three identities involve squaring trigonometric functions.
DISCUSSION
Just as X times X is X , cos q times cos q is (cos q) .
(X)(X) = (X)2 = (X)2 = X2 (cos q)(cos q) = (cos q)2 = cos2qq)2
The only difference is that trigonometric functions often show the power near the function itself, but using parentheses is also acceptable.
(X)(X) = (X)2 = (X)2 = X2 (cos q)(cos q) = (cos q)2 = cos2qq)2
This avoids any confusion between squaring the angle or squaring the function.
cos(q)(q) = cos q2 (cos q)(cos q) = (cos q)2 = cos2qos2qqq
The first identity is called the Pythagorean Identity and is based on the Pythagorean Theorem.
Both sides of the Pythagorean Theorem are divided by c .
Notice that side b is opposite angle q and side a is adjacent q.
The equation is rewritten as shown since sin q is the value of the opposite side over the hypotenuse and cos q is the value of the adjacent side over the hypotenuse.
The remaining two identities are found by using the Pythagorean Identity.
Both sides of the Pythagorean Identity are divided by cos
The equation can be rewritten as shown since sin q/cos q is tan q and 1/cos q is sec q.
The last identity is found by dividing both sides of the Pythagorean Identity by sin
The equation can be rewritten as shown since cos q/sin q is cot q and 1/sin q is csc q.
Each trigonometric function can be rewritten in terms of a different trigonometric function by using the identities and a little imagination.
